newsitem.title: PERU: Peru defense head resigns in crisis - sources.
newsitem.headline: Peru defense head resigns in crisis - sources.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori's cabinet suffered another loss on Thursday with the resignation of Defence Minister Gen. Tomas Castillo Meza over rights abuses by the security forces, government sources said.
Castillo's departure, which could not be immediately confirmed by official government spokesmen, followed Wednesday's resignation of Foreign Minister Francisco Tudela.
Tudela, one of the most respected figures in the cabinet, was widely believed to have resigned to disassociate himself from a string of embarrassing scandals facing Fujimori.
The sources said the defence post would be filled by Interior Minister Gen. Cesar Saucedo Sanchez, who in turn would be replaced by regional military head Gen. Jose Villanueva Ruesta.
There were unconfirmed versions in local media that Justice Minister Carlos Hermoza Moya had also had a resignation offer accepted by Fujimori.

The apparent cabinet changes deepened a political crisis that has seen Fujimori's popularity tumble to its lowest level in seven years of power on growing public outrage over a series of allegations against the government aired in the media.

Particularly damaging were weekend claims of phone-tapping by secret services, and the annulment of Peruvian citizenship for the Israeli-born owner of a local television channel critical of the security forces.
The allegation believed to have brought Meza's departure was the recent torture of army intelligence agent Leonor La Rosa by colleagues angry at her alleged leaks to the media.
Peru's entire cabinet had made a technical resignation last week as part of a routine annual move ahead of the president's speech to the nation on the July 28 Independence Day.

The president normally ratifies his ministers or makes changes on that day. But analysts said this week's moves showed senior government figures were taking the initiative to resign irrevocably rather than wait for Fujimori's decision.
